 Judgment
This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 02.02.2021 at about 02.45 p.m he was proceeding on Bike bearing No.KA66H 2256 from his native Kenchapura Village to Gowarapura to harvest Arecanuts as he is doing Arecanut business with his father for his livelihood and when he reached near Kudakere Village Cross Road, at that time from opposite direction the driver of Mahindra Bolero Pick Up Car bearing No.KA18C5498 driven by respondent No.1,
in rash and negligent manner and dashed against bike of the petitioner.

Due to this the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to Nanjappa hospital, Shivamogga and admitted as inpatient for 6 days and underwent surgery and spent more than a sum of Rs.3,50,000/ towards medical expenses and prior to the accident the petitioner was working as Agriculturist and Arecanut business and was earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he is not able to do any normal work and cannot concentrate on his business and suffering from physically and financially.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Car driver and Channagiri Police have registered a case against the driver of the said offending Car.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the said offending Car and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a with costs.
03.
On service of notice, the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their counsel and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending car, age, income,
occupation of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and contended that alleged accident is not occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.KA18C5498 and it is due to rash and negligent riding of said twowheeler bearing No.KA66H2256 at the time of crossing of the road.

This respondent has denied the alleged accident,
negligence of the driver of offending car, age, income, occupation of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and contended that Mahindra Bolero Pick Up vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and alleged accident is not occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Mahindra Bolero vehicle bearing No.KA18C5498 and it is the negligence of the claimant who was riding the Motor Cycle.

There is a delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint and the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident and the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective defendant as on the date of accident and thereby the owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
There is no valid permit and FC to the offending Car as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.
(SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 06. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my predecessor has framed the following Issues: ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 02.02.2021 at about 02.45 p.m. on Kodakikere village, Channagiri Taluk, Davanagere District, due to rash and negligent act of the driving of the Bolero vehicle bearing registration No.KA18C5498 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03

. What Order or Award?
07.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents as Ex.P.1 to 10 and two witnesses is examined as PW.2 and 3 and through them Ex.P.11 to 19 documents are marked and closed the petitioner side evidence.
On the otherhand the respondents did not lead evidence and hence the respondents evidence is taken as nil.
(SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 08. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the respondents and perused the records.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:
The petitioner in order to prove his case he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

In the cross examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that his father was lodged complaint to the Police and there was no impediment for his parents to lodge complaint immediately after the accident.

In wound certificate the name of Sunil is mentioned as accompanied by him and his father name is not mentioned and denied to the suggestion that he himself fell down and sustained injuries and the bolero vehicle was not involved in the accident and his father after 03 days of accident in (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 collusion with RC owner of bolero vehicle register false case against the respondent No.2 and his father is the friend of RC owner of bolero vehicle and false case is registered and also denied to the suggestion that on the date of accident he did not wore helmet and if at all he wore helmet on the date of accident no injuries were sustained to his head and denied to the suggestion that he fit and fine as earlier and having no difficulties and also denied to the suggestion that as the accident road is in repair, he rode the motor cycle in rash manner and caused accident and the accident took place due to his negligence.
11.

Further, PW.2 who is Supervisor at Nanjappa hospital, Shivamogga, has produced MLC extract,
Police intimation, Entire Case sheet and Xray pertaining to the petitioner at Ex.P.12 to 15 and in the crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that in Ex.P.12 the vehicle number is not mentioned and denied to the suggestion that in order to help the petitioner, he has created the documents 12.

Further, PW.3 is a Doctor and Neuro Surgeon, who examined the petitioner and Neuro Psychological assessment was done by him and has stated that as per CT brain the petitioner sustained large right frontal and right temporal extradural (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 hematoma and he assessed neurological disability of around 15% and said disability pertains to whole body and likely to be permanent and has produced OPD records, Neuro psychological reports,
Mini mental state examination report and Skull Xray report with film as per Ex.P.16 to 19.

During the course of cross examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and he examined the petitioner 3 years after accident and he has not taken opinion of the treated doctor and the petitioner has not produced any document before him to show he is taken treatment at Neuro Bharat hospital and external injuries are healed up but internal injuries are not completely healed up and admits that blood clot in the brain was removed.

Partially injury was healed up and admits that except said injury treatment no other treatment has given to the petitioner and denied to the suggestion that petitioner has not got any difficulties as stated in his Akash K.E vs Kubera H on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9074626/
4 affidavit, he has not used Nimhans battery while assessing disability and denied to the suggestion that if he has used Nimhans battery test, petitioner has not got any disability and also denied to the suggestion that there is no difficulties for day to day work of petitioner and he has assessed only neuro disability (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 and denied to the suggestion that since he has not treated doctor he has not competent to assess disability and also admits that he has not refer the petitioner to the Medical Board.
13.

sentences.text: Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Channagiri Police against the driver of the offending car.
Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against driver of the offending car for his rash and negligent driving and caused the accident.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Charge Sheet which was filed against the driver/respondent No.1 of the offending car.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Spot Mahazar.

Ex.P.5 is copy of Spot Sketch which indicates that the accident occurred head on collusion and offending vehicle was came to the extreme right side and dashed against the Motor Cycle of the petitioner and caused accident.
Ex.P.6 is copy of IMV report which indicates that both vehicles are involved in the accident and front portion of both vehicles are damaged.

Ex.P.7 is Discharge summary discloses that the petitioner was admitted to Nanjappa Multi Speciality hospital, Shivamogga from 02.02.2021 to 07.02.2021 wherein he was treated as inpatient for 6 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.8 is Final bill amounting to (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 Rs.1,16,730/.
Ex . P.9
is Medical bills amounting to Rs.30,155/.
Ex . P.10
is copy
of Wound certificate which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident
. Ex.P.12 is MLC extract.
Ex.P.13 is Police intimation.
Ex . P.14
is entire
Case sheet
. Ex.P.15 is Xray.
Ex.P.16 is OPD records.
Ex.P.17 is Neuro psychological reports.
Ex.P.18 is Mini mental state examination report and Ex.P.19 is Skull Xray report with film.

14. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has proved and established that he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 02.02.2021 at about 02.45 p.m on Kenchapura Village to Gowarapura, near Kudakere Village Cross Road, due to rash and negligent driving of Mahindra Pick Up Car bearing No.KA18C5498 by its driver as alleged in the petition.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved the Issue No.1.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 20 years and working as Agriculturist and Arecanut business and was earning Rs.25,000/ p.m and has incurred Rs.3,50,000/ towards medical expenses, food, nourishment,
conveyance and attendant charges etc., and became permanent disablement.

It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth and not produced any documents to show his avocation and income.
On perusal of medical records and Police records, it appears that the petitioner is aged about 20 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 20 years and as per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Akash K.E vs Kubera H on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9074626/
5

sentences.text:
Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 18 to 25 is 18.
16.
With regard to his avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 to go by the LokAdalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2021 to be taken as Rs.15,000/ p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,000/.
17.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner sustained large right frontal and right temporal extradural hematoma.
According to assessment of said doctor total disability of around 15% and said disability pertains to whole body and likely to be permanent.

But on perusal of evidence of PW.1 who himself appeared before the tribunal and gave evidence and he has properly answered to the questions put to him in the crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel before the tribunal.
Hence, it is not appears that the petitioner sustained neuro disability of 15% and he has not produced any evidence or documents regarding 15% of his physical functional disability.
The neuro disability assessed by the doctor may not come in the way of his day to day work.

However, considering the evidence of PW.3 and the medical records at Ex.P.16 to 19, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.
(SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;
15,000/ x 12 x 18 x 10% = Rs.3,24,000/.
18.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 Discharge summary, according to which he was admitted in the hospital as inpatient for 6 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.

19. Pain and sufferings: As per Ex.P.10 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.3 doctor and as per Ex.P.14 to 19 Case sheet, Xray, OPD records, Neuro psychological reports, Mini mental state examination report and Skull Xray report with film which indicates that on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and as per Ex.P.10 Wound certificate petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.
20. Loss of income during laid up period:

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,000/ p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 6 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months.

Thus, taking Akash K.E vs Kubera H on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9074626/
6 into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.30,000/
(Rs.15,000 x 2) under this head.

sentences.text: 21. Medical expenses: As per Ex.P.8 is Final bill amounting to Rs.1,16,730/ and Ex.P.9
Medical bills amounting to Rs.30,155/ and total will be Rs.1,46,885/.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,46,885/ under the head of medical expenses.
22. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/ towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
23. Future medical expenses:
The doctor PW.3 who assessed neuro disability has not stated anything about future medical expenses of the petitioner and he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding future medical expenses, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

24. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 3,24,00000 2.
Pain and Sufferings 30,00000 3.
Attendant charges, extra 30,00000 nutritious food and conveyance charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,46,88500 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,00000 unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 30,00000 period Total 5,90,88500 (SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 25.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,90,885/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

26. Though the respondents have taken several defences in their written statement, but they have n ot lead their defence evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and despite so many opportunities they have not lead any rebuttal evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner.

According to written statement of respondent No.1, he is the owner of the Mahindra Pick Up Car and it is duly insured with respondent No.2 and insurance policy is valid as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para No.2 has admits that it has issued insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle and as on the date of accident Akash K.E vs Kubera H on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9074626/
7
the insurance policy is valid and is in force and no material on record to show that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated any terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending Car and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay (SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay compensation of Rs.5,90,885/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,90,885/ (Rupees Five lakhs ninety thousand eight hundred and eighty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through Epayment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account (SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.3016/2021 details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para No.2 has admits that it has issued insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle and as on the date of accident Akash K.E vs Kubera H on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9074626/
7
the insurance policy is valid and is in force and no material on record to show that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated any terms and conditions of the policy.
